title: Customer registration, login and basket

sourcesRead.contributes: context, AC-1..AC-6, out of scope, PO comment with the password rules, test data
endpoints (register, security questions, login, add basket item, read basket, products), request/response bodies, Bearer auth, duplicate e-mail error

context: A visitor can become a customer by registering, then log in to receive an authentication token, and use that token to manage their shopping basket. Each customer has exactly one basket. The story covers the registration rules, the login token, adding an item to one's own basket, and the isolation between different customers' baskets. Registration and login details are in attachment api-contract.md; the password rules are clarified in the product owner's comment.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Registering with a unique e-mail, a rule-compliant password (sent as both `password` and `passwordRepeat`), and a security question id + security answer creates the customer: the response is **HTTP 201** and its body describes the new user with the submitted `email` and `role` = `customer`.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Registering with an e-mail that already belongs to a customer is rejected with **HTTP 400** and a validation error whose message states the e-mail must be unique. No second account is created.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Registration enforces the password rules in the PO comment: a password shorter than the minimum length is rejected with **HTTP 400** and the customer is **not** created (a follow-up login with that e-mail/password fails).

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Basket contents are private to their owner: a customer must be able to read only their **own** basket. A request to `GET /rest/basket/{id}` authenticated as customer A but targeting customer B's basket id must be refused and must not return B's basket. Verify with two customers you create.

auth.mechanism: Authorization: Bearer <token>, the JWT `token` returned by POST /rest/user/login
auth.credentials: customers the tests register themselves with a unique e-mail per run; the password comes from the environment variable JS_USER_PASSWORD

rules.text: Each customer has exactly one basket.

The password must be at least 5 characters long (and at most 40). Anything shorter than 5 characters must be rejected at registration and the account not created; a 3- or 4-character password is a clear reject case.
The password is case-sensitive and stored hashed (not tested here beyond that a too-short password is refused).

errorModel.case: registering an e-mail that already belongs to a customer
errorModel.body: a validation error whose message states the e-mail must be unique

errorModel.case: registering with a password shorter than 5 characters
reading another customer's basket (GET /rest/basket/{id} as customer A with customer B's basket id): refused, B's basket not returned (status not stated, see G4)

testData.strategy: tests create their own customers with a unique e-mail per run (POST /api/Users); the password is provided out of band via the environment variable JS_USER_PASSWORD, a value that satisfies the password rules
constraints: JS_USER_PASSWORD is well above the 5-character minimum (story.md#L53-L54)
valid security-question ids come from GET /api/SecurityQuestions
valid product ids come from GET /api/Products (existing catalogue, not seeded)
AC-6 is verified with two customers the tests create

outOfScope: Checkout and payment; coupons; password reset; the "Remember me" option; deleting a basket item.
Password case-sensitivity and hashed storage: "not our concern to test here beyond that a too-short password is refused" (story.md#L51)
